meta.label: Volunteering
tradeoffLabels: easy to start with a simple sign-up
little personal data or screening required to begin
meta.attribution: Facts here come from each organization's own volunteering, screening or background-check page, read directly, plus the National Park Service's official Reference Manual 7 for its Volunteers-in-Parks program, Login.gov's own account help for the federal Volunteer.gov portal, the Arizona Supreme Court's CASA program page for CASA/GAL volunteer requirements, and the European Commission's European Youth Portal for the European Solidarity Corps. Accessibility describes how much stands between deciding to help and actually starting: an application, an interview, a minimum term, a criminal history check. Privacy describes how much personal data that route requires you to hand over to begin, from just an email address up to a Social Security number and fingerprints. Neither score is a judgment of the organization's mission or the value of the work; a route that screens hard usually does so because it puts volunteers in sustained, unsupervised contact with children, elderly people or people with disabilities, and the screening exists to protect them, not to inconvenience the volunteer. Several organizations run tiered systems where a single event needs almost nothing and an ongoing or higher-trust role needs a full background check; where that is true, the note says so and the score reflects the more common, lower-commitment route into that organization. Two entries, DoSomething.org and JustServe, plus Idealist, describe their own sign-up process as an account and a listing, with no screening step described at the platform level; that description is the evidence for a high score, not an audit of the thousands of organizations each one lists. Ways to help describes the breadth of distinct opportunities a route actually offers, which is unscored wherever no organization published a concrete figure for it. Giving money instead of time is a different decision, covered under Causes to support and Crowdfunding platforms. Suggest changes via Contribute.

criteria.label: Easy to start, without a lengthy application or minimum term
Little personal data or background screening required to begin
Breadth of distinct volunteer opportunities on offer

products.name: Idealist (formerly VolunteerMatch)
products.description: A merged nonprofit and volunteer-opportunity board, after VolunteerMatch became part of Idealist in early 2025. Lists a large number of listings across many cause areas, virtual and in person, through a free account.

accessibility.note: Idealist's VolunteerMatch page states VolunteerMatch became part of Idealist 'in early 2025' and describes finding opportunities and applying through the site; volunteermatch.org itself now redirects permanently to this Idealist page.

ways_to_help.note: The page states the combined platform offers '100,000+ unique ways to volunteer, with opportunities for virtual and onsite opportunities to support 56 different cause areas.'

products.name: JustServe
products.description: A free volunteer-matching site and app run by The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, open to anyone regardless of faith, connecting people to local community service projects posted by other organizations.

accessibility.note: JustServe's about page states 'JustServe is free for all users, organizations and volunteers' and that creating an account is done through the website or app, with the site stating 'everyone is invited to use JustServe, regardless of their race, religion, gender, ethnicity, or sexual orientation.'

privacy.note: The about page describes registering an account and customizing a profile to match skills and interests with posted projects; it does not describe a background check or other screening step at the JustServe platform level, distinct from whatever the individual project's host organization may separately require.

products.name: AmeriCorps
products.description: A US national service program placing members in full-time or part-time community roles for a set term, with a living allowance and an education award in return. Positions with recurring access to children, older adults or people with disabilities require a criminal history check before service starts.

accessibility.note: AmeriCorps' own National Service Criminal History Checks page states three checks are required before an eligible person may begin serving: a National Sex Offender Public Website check, a state criminal history check, and an FBI fingerprint-based check, all completed and reviewed no later than the day before service begins.

privacy.note: The same page states the process includes an FBI fingerprint-based check conducted through an AmeriCorps-approved vendor, and that applicants submit a copy of government-issued identification along with a set of fingerprints as part of the National Service Criminal History Check.

ways_to_help.note: The page's own navigation lists several distinct AmeriCorps program tracks that fall under national service, including AmeriCorps State/National, AmeriCorps VISTA, and AmeriCorps Seniors' RSVP, Foster Grandparent and Senior Companion programs, each with its own eligibility path.

products.name: Peace Corps
products.description: A US federal program placing volunteers abroad for a roughly 27-month assignment across sectors including agriculture, education, health, environment and community development. Every invitee goes through a background investigation and a full medical clearance before departing.

accessibility.note: Peace Corps' legal clearance page states 'the Peace Corps is required to complete a background investigation on all applicants' and that once conditionally invited, an applicant receives 'guidance on submitting fingerprints and the background investigation certification form' before they can depart for service.

privacy.note: The same page states full disclosure of legal history is required, including any citation, arrest or charge regardless of outcome, and that fingerprints are submitted as part of the background investigation certification process; non-disclosure alone can result in a rescinded invitation.

ways_to_help.note: The Peace Corps site's own navigation lists six work sectors volunteers are placed in: Agriculture, Community Economic Development, Education, Environment, Health, and Youth in Development.

products.name: Habitat for Humanity
products.description: Builds and repairs homes with volunteer labor alongside future homeowners. Most build-day volunteers only need to register and sign a waiver; a background check applies to four specific roles, including trip team leaders and Disaster Corps volunteers.

accessibility.note: Habitat for Humanity International's own background-check FAQ, still the version it publishes (marked 'Reviewed by Habitat Legal Department 10/07/2019', with no newer edition found on habitat.org), states the screening policy adopted June 1, 2019 applies specifically to '(1) trip team leaders, (2) Care-A-Vanners, (3) Disaster Corps volunteers and (4) AmeriCorps host site managers,' meaning most day-to-day build volunteers are not in a role the policy covers.

privacy.note: For the roles the policy does cover, the same still-published FAQ states an applicant provides 'full legal name, date of birth, social security number, phone number, email and address history' to Habitat's background-check vendor Asurint, and that credit checks are not included, so most build-day volunteers outside those four roles are not asked for this information.

ways_to_help.note: Habitat's volunteer hub lists distinct routes in: local volunteering near you (Women Build, Home Preservation, Veterans Build, Youth Programs), travel-and-build programs (Global Village, RV Care-A-Vanners, Collegiate Challenge, Habitat and Thrivent), long-term service in the United States, internationally and through AmeriCorps, group opportunities for businesses, faith partners and community organizations, and build events such as World Habitat Day.

products.name: American Red Cross
products.description: Runs disaster response, blood drives and safety training through local volunteers. Applying means creating a Volunteer Connection profile, and a background check is a standard step before a role is assigned, not a special case.

accessibility.note: The Red Cross's Virginia volunteer FAQ, on the national redcross.org domain, describes the steps as entering a zip code, applying to an opportunity, creating a Volunteer Connection account, and states 'once you have completed the application process and background check, a volunteer Engagement Specialist will contact you' to finalize a match.

privacy.note: The same FAQ states disaster response applicants 'will also be required to submit a background check' as part of the standard application through Volunteer Connection, ahead of being matched with an Engagement Specialist.

products.name: Special Olympics
products.description: Provides year-round sports training and competition for people with intellectual disabilities. Under the national US rules, coaches, drivers and others in close athlete contact give references, answer screening questions and authorize a criminal background check; single-day volunteers can register on the day with just their name, address and phone number.

accessibility.note: Section 3.14 of Special Olympics, Inc.'s US-specific supplement to its General Rules, which sets the screening rules for its US state programs, states that 'Class C volunteers may register on the same day of their participation (but before that participation begins)', Class C being those who volunteer 'for a single day or a single event'; all volunteers must still review written conduct information before taking part. These are national minimums, and state programs can add steps (Special Olympics Texas, for example, also asks day-of-event volunteers for a photo ID check).

privacy.note: The same section states Class C volunteers give only 'their full name, complete address, telephone number', while Class A and Class B volunteers must add photo identification, 'at least two personal references who are not family members' and written answers on drug use, criminal convictions, abuse charges and license suspensions, and Class A volunteers (coaches, drivers, overnight hosts and those with fiscal authority) must also give 'written authorization to the U.S. Program for the conduct of a criminal background check'.

links.label: US-specific General Rules, Section 3.14 volunteer screening (Special Olympics, Inc.)
Volunteer Screening Policy (Special Olympics Texas, a stricter state implementation)

products.name: DoSomething.org
products.description: A campaign platform for people age 13 to 25 to take specific social-change actions on climate, safety and equity, ranging from short one-time actions to sustained projects, with no age ceiling enforced beyond the stated range.

accessibility.note: DoSomething's about page states 'if you're 13-25, there's a space for you at our table' and describes the platform as a coach, champion and connector helping members take pledges and complete actions and campaigns.

privacy.note: The about page describes taking a pledge and completing a documented action, such as an 'action streak,' as the participation model; it does not describe a background check or screening step for taking part in a campaign.

products.name: Big Brothers Big Sisters
products.description: Matches an adult volunteer mentor with a child for a sustained one-on-one relationship. Becoming a mentor means a written application, reference checks, an in-person interview and a background check before being matched.

accessibility.note: Big Brothers Big Sisters of America's national safeguarding page states its 'National Standards of Excellence require each volunteer to complete an extensive screening process,' naming a written application, background and reference checks, and an in-person interview as required steps before a match, on top of orientation and training.

privacy.note: The same page confirms background and reference checks are a required part of that national screening process for every volunteer, in addition to the in-person interview, before a mentoring match is made.

products.name: National Park Service Volunteers-in-Parks
products.description: Places volunteers in national parks for anything from a single trail day to a long-term assignment. Short-term, episodic volunteering uses a simpler sign-up form; longer assignments can call for more paperwork, including background checks for certain roles.

accessibility.note: The NPS's Reference Manual 7, Chapter 5, distinguishes short-term or episodic volunteering, which uses the simpler OF301a individual form (or OF301b for a group led by one signed form), from long-term volunteering, and states that after the volunteer service agreement is signed, a park 'may require the volunteer's signature on additional written documentation or forms that pertain to their assignment,' including background-check forms.

privacy.note: The same chapter states additional forms tied to a specific assignment 'may include forms for background checks, PIV issuance, vehicle usage, credentialing, training certifications,' indicating background screening applies to some roles and assignments rather than to every Volunteers-in-Parks sign-up.

links.label: Reference Manual 7, Chapter 5: Onboarding and Management

products.name: Meals on Wheels America
products.description: Connects people to a local Meals on Wheels provider to deliver meals to homebound neighbors, usually using the volunteer's own car. Screening is set locally rather than nationally, so what is required varies by provider.

accessibility.note: Meals on Wheels America's volunteer page states the sign-up step is to 'fill out the signup form above, and we'll share contact information for a local Meals on Wheels provider in your area,' after which the volunteer contacts that provider directly to discuss the role.

privacy.note: The same page states 'the vetting process for volunteers varies by location,' and that volunteers 'may be asked to undergo a background check process prior to volunteering,' so the personal information required is set by the local provider rather than being uniform nationwide.

products.name: Points of Light
products.description: A global network of affiliate volunteer-mobilizing organizations, searchable by region and cause through its own engagement platform, connecting people to opportunities run by its member organizations rather than running programs itself.

accessibility.note: Points of Light's engagement platform, Points of Light Engage, describes itself as pulling 'volunteer opportunities from sites around the web' into one database, and states 'Individuals can search for volunteer projects, nonprofits can post and manage event sign-ups, and visitors are invited to start projects of their own', with a keyword and optional location search on its front page; its global network directory separately lets people find a local affiliate by location, focus area and services.

ways_to_help.note: Points of Light's home page currently gives its global impact figures as '120' 'Nonprofits in Our Global Network' and '32' 'Countries with Points of Light Programs', plus '3M' 'Volunteers engaged in 2024'; the volunteer count is the latest year it reports.

products.name: Crisis Text Line
products.description: A US text-message crisis service staffed by trained volunteer Crisis Counselors who work remotely, supported by trained supervisors on every shift. Becoming one means an online application, a free 15-hour training course, a background check and a 200-hour commitment.

accessibility.note: Crisis Text Line's volunteer page sets out three steps: create an account and complete an application of about 20 minutes (applicants must be at least 18), complete a free, self-paced 15-hour online training over a two-week cohort, then take a first shift; it states 'Volunteer Crisis Counselors commit to 200 hours of conversations with people in need.' Volunteering is fully remote and flexible, but the training and the 200-hour commitment put it close to Red Cross and well above a single-event sign-up.

privacy.note: The same page states 'The completion of a background check is also part of the training process', assessed against what it calls fair and narrowly tailored criteria, on top of the account and written application. A background check is required of every counselor, so scored level with the Red Cross's standard background check.

products.name: Samaritans
products.description: Runs a 24-hour listening service across the UK and Ireland, answered by trained volunteers in more than 200 branches, alongside volunteers who support events, fundraising and branch work. Every role involves recruitment and training, and the listening role requires a criminal record check.

accessibility.note: Samaritans' volunteering page answers 'Can I start straight away?' with 'No.', explaining that all volunteers undergo recruitment and training in all roles and that 'our volunteering is not something you can start immediately'. Its listening volunteer page adds an interview, training over 5 to 10 sessions that typically takes a few months, a minimum age of 18, a usual commitment of one 3 to 4 hour shift a week plus periodic night shifts, and an expectation that the role is long term.

privacy.note: Samaritans' listening volunteer page states that, to safeguard volunteers and callers, the listening role requires a criminal record check. Samaritans' Criminal Records Vetting Policy explains these are DBS checks, or the Disclosure Scotland/PVG, Access Northern Ireland and Garda Vetting equivalents, completed after selection in the early stages of training, and that 'Criminal record checks will be repeated at a maximum of three-year intervals'. A record does not automatically bar an applicant; each case is assessed.

ways_to_help.note: Samaritans' volunteering page names three routes: listening volunteers answering calls and messages from one of 201 branches, events volunteers supporting fundraisers at events like the London Marathon, and support volunteers helping branches with marketing, fundraising, events, IT or in its shops.

products.name: Zooniverse
products.description: A people-powered research platform run by a collaboration of UK and US institutions, where volunteers classify images, sounds and records for real research projects in astronomy, ecology, history and more, from any computer or phone.

accessibility.note: Zooniverse's How to volunteer page says becoming a volunteer is easy, just start classifying, that everyone who contributes to a project is a volunteer, and that there is no minimum time requirement: you can do as much or as little as you like. Its About page adds that no specialized background, training or expertise is needed. Registering is encouraged for stats, a volunteer certificate and the Talk boards, with a parent or guardian signing off for anyone under 16.

privacy.note: Zooniverse's standard project FAQ (shown here on the Old Weather WW2 project) answers the question of why to register by stating that you do not need to create an account to take part in Zooniverse projects, and that you can take part anonymously with your answers still saved and used in the research; an account only adds classification counts, Talk discussion and email updates.

ways_to_help.note: Zooniverse's projects page listed 70 active projects in October 2026, filterable across 11 disciplines: arts, biology, climate, history, language, literature, medicine, nature, physics, social science and space, from camera-trap surveys and herbarium digitisation to galaxy classification.

links.label: Project FAQ: do I need an account?

products.name: Catchafire
products.description: Matches professionals with US nonprofits for skills-based projects, from a one-hour consultation call to a project of up to 50 hours, in areas such as marketing, IT and finance. Volunteers apply to projects and the nonprofit decides whether to work with them.

accessibility.note: Catchafire's volunteer page describes the route as browse, apply, then match once both the volunteer and the nonprofit decide it is a good fit, with projects ranging from 5 to 50 hours, one-hour consultation calls and 15-minute quick advice for those with less time. Its FAQ explains a short application is required even though the work is unpaid, recommends applying to 2 to 4 projects at once to maximize the chance of a match, and mentions interviewing with the nonprofit. An application and a selection step, but no minimum term beyond the project you choose.

privacy.note: The page states volunteers 'Submit your application and resume to let the nonprofit know you are interested', and the FAQ says to expect to give some information upfront about why you are interested and how your expertise can help. That is a professional profile and work history shared with the nonprofit; no background check is described. Scored between Meals on Wheels' locally set vetting and Special Olympics' single-day details.

ways_to_help.note: The page states volunteers can choose from over 150 project types, 24 different cause areas and 35 skill sets, plus one-hour calls, quick advice and nonprofit board matching, and reports 67K+ volunteer-nonprofit matches to date.

products.name: Feeding America food banks
products.description: The national network of US food banks, food pantries and meal programs. Its volunteer page points people to a local member food bank, where most volunteering is a sign-up for a sorting, packing or distribution shift.

accessibility.note: Feeding America's volunteer page describes three steps: find a food bank in the Feeding America network with its search tool, sign up for a shift, and show up; it states 'Most food banks list their available volunteer shifts on their website.' Any screening is set by the individual food bank, and the national page does not describe one, so no privacy score is given.

ways_to_help.note: The page lists four kinds of food bank volunteering, food sorting and packing, shopping assistance for families, home delivery driving for elderly or disabled neighbors, and cooking and meal prep, plus three other ways to help: hosting a food drive, donating and fundraising.

products.name: Volunteer.gov
products.description: The US federal government's volunteer portal, listing opportunities at sites run by agencies including the National Park Service, Fish & Wildlife Service and Bureau of Land Management, from one-day events to seasonal resident positions. Applying needs a Login.gov account.

accessibility.note: Volunteer.gov's home page asks people to sign in with Login.gov and submit a volunteer application to the site they choose, with filtered searches for virtual volunteering, one-day events and positions that offer lodging; its latest listings in October 2026 ran from a National Public Lands Day clean-up to campground host and refuge resident positions lasting several months. A sign-in and an application for each role, with the hosting agency deciding, places it near the National Park Service's own route.

privacy.note: Login.gov's help page on creating an account lists the steps: an email address you confirm, a password of 12 or more characters, and a required second authentication method (multi-factor authentication); the steps listed do not include identity verification. What a hosting agency then asks for in its application, including any background check for a particular position, varies by role and is not counted here.

ways_to_help.note: The home page states volunteers can submit an application to thousands of sites across the country, all at federal agencies, and offers filtered searches for virtual volunteering, one-day events, lodging-offered positions, education and outreach, hands-on work and natural-resource care.

links.label: Login.gov: how do I create an account

products.name: European Solidarity Corps
products.description: The European Union's volunteering programme for people aged 18 to 30 (35 for humanitarian aid), placing them in funded projects abroad or at home, individually or in teams, for anything from two weeks to a year, with travel, accommodation and food covered.

accessibility.note: The European Youth Portal's volunteering page states the programme is for '18-30 year old people who reside in one of the EU countries and other countries covered', that individual volunteering lasts between 2 weeks and 12 months and team volunteering between 2 weeks and 2 months, both full-time at 30 to 38 hours a week, and that individual volunteering abroad needs both a support and a host organisation. It adds that registering does not guarantee a place. The age band, the full-time term and the two-organisation match keep it among the harder routes to start.

privacy.note: The registration page states you first create an EU Login account, verify it by email, set a password and 'Make sure to enable the Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) after the password is set - this is mandatory', then complete a European Solidarity Corps profile. No background check is described at registration; what a host organisation asks for later is set by that organisation.

ways_to_help.note: The Corps' About page names the routes in: volunteering abroad solo or in a team, setting up your own Solidarity Project in your community, and Humanitarian Aid Volunteering, open up to age 35.

products.name: Reach Volunteering
products.description: A UK charity matching people with professional experience to skills-based volunteer roles and trustee positions at charities, free for volunteers. It had announced plans to close, then said it will stay open after nine funders and donors stepped in.

accessibility.note: Reach's home page states 'If you have three years’ professional experience and are based in the UK, you can apply for opportunities on Reach', searching by skills, interests, availability and location, and it also carries the notice 'Reach is staying open' after a collaboration of nine funders and donors reversed its planned closure. Open only to experienced professionals, then an application to each organisation.

ways_to_help.note: Reach's guide to skills-based volunteering states it has 'thousands of opportunities available on our online platform', across skills such as HR, digital, finance and marketing, including trustee roles, and its home page reports 5,996 people placed in trustee or volunteer roles in 2025. Breadth is wide but limited to skills-based and governance roles.

products.name: Doit Life
products.description: A UK volunteering database, run by the social enterprise Doit Life jointly with the Doit Foundation, where a free account lets people search opportunities posted by national charities and local community groups.

accessibility.note: Doit Life's volunteer page describes a FREE Doit Life account that connects people to its database of volunteer opportunities, and its home page states the platform is completely free for members of the public; signing up and searching is the whole first step, with any screening set by the charity offering a role. Scored level with Idealist.

ways_to_help.note: The volunteer page invites people to 'Browse thousands of volunteer opportunities' from national charities and community groups, and Doit's home page reports 60,000 non-profits supported and 1 million user accounts created since 2002. No exact live count of listings is published, so scored below Idealist's stated 100,000+.

products.name: Be My Eyes
products.description: A free app that connects blind and low-vision people to sighted volunteers by live video, so a volunteer can describe what the camera shows. Calls are short and a volunteer only answers when free.

accessibility.note: Be My Eyes' Volunteer Hub explains that when a blind or low-vision user asks for help, a notification goes to several volunteers at once and you answer only if you are available, that calls are short and casual, and that 'You’ll only receive calls in your daytime hours (8am to 9pm)' in your own language. There is no minimum commitment, and it warns that with far more volunteers than users it is normal to wait a while for a call.

privacy.note: Be My Eyes' privacy policy (effective September 1, 2026) states that when you register through the app it collects your name, your email address and your preferred language(s), and uses location and language information to route calls to an appropriate time zone; it records whether you chose the volunteer path. No screening or background check is described. During a call the volunteer shares audio, not video. Scored level with DoSomething.org's account-only route.

products.name: CASA/GAL volunteer advocate
products.description: Court Appointed Special Advocate (CASA) and guardian ad litem (GAL) volunteers are appointed by judges to advocate for children who have experienced abuse or neglect, staying with a case until the child has a safe, permanent home. Programs are run locally under the National CASA/GAL Association.

accessibility.note: The National CASA/GAL Association's page on its model states volunteers are rigorously screened and trained by their local program, that 'Each volunteer receives more than 30 hours of training before they work with a child', with an additional 12 hours of continued education every year, and that volunteers stay with each case until it is closed. Court appointment, a training course and a case that lasts until permanency make this one of the most demanding routes here, alongside AmeriCorps and the Peace Corps.

privacy.note: The Arizona Supreme Court's CASA of Arizona page, which carries the National CASA Association's volunteer information, lists the requirements as being 21 years old, being willing to 'complete necessary background checks, provide references and participate in an interview', completing at least 30 hours of pre-service training and being available for court appearances; it puts the average case at about a year and a half. Background checks, references and an interview match the Big Brothers Big Sisters screening.

links.label: Volunteer as a CASA (Arizona Supreme Court)

products.name: parkrun volunteering
products.description: Free, weekly, timed 5k walks and runs in parks, run entirely by volunteers who set up the course, marshal, time and scan barcodes. Anyone can volunteer, and no experience or previous visit is needed.

accessibility.note: parkrun's volunteer page states 'There’s no experience needed and you don’t need to have been to a parkrun before', that someone will show you what to do on the day, and that if you do not want to commit in advance you can 'just turn up to your local event and talk to the volunteers when you arrive'. It reports over 40,000 people volunteering at parkrun each week.

privacy.note: To volunteer in advance, the same page asks you to email your local event: 'Please include your full name and, if you know it, your parkrun ID found on your barcode.' A parkrun registration covers walking, running and volunteering alike, with no separate volunteer registration, and the page describes no background check, except for additional requirements at junior parkrun in Australia.
